Retry-After.description: Seconds until the next write is accepted

Forbidden.description: The caller's role does not allow this, or a password check is due.

RateLimited.description: More than 20 requests a second from this caller (token, user or socket; bursts of 100); try again after `Retry-After` seconds.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until the next request is accepted

WrongStage.description: The session is not at the stage this step needs, for example already logged in.

Access.description:
What a caller may do, in increasing order. `metrics` reads `/metrics` only, for
Prometheus; the others are the user roles.

AuditRecord.description: One audit record; `prev` is the SHA-256 of the record before it.

CreatedToken.description: A new token: the value is shown only in this answer.

error.description: What went wrong, in a sentence.

Owned.description: One object and the provider that owns it, secrets masked.

Role.description: What a user may do (ADR-0024, "What each role may do").

csrf_token.description: Send it in `X-CSRF-Token` with every unsafe request.

Stage.description: How far a session has come.

allowed_from.description: Networks the token may be used from; empty means anywhere.

expires_in_days.description: Days until it expires; `0` never, when `admin.tokens.allow_no_expiry` allows it.

reset_mfa.description: Removes the user's second factor, so they enrol again at the next login.

redact.description: Header names whose values are replaced by `***`.

sample.description:
Share of successful requests (status below 400) that are logged, from 0 to 1. Errors
and failed requests are always logged.

ca.description: Certificate authority: a known name or an `https://` ACME directory URL.

ca_root.description:
PEM file with the root certificate of a CA whose ACME endpoint is not publicly trusted,
such as an internal step-ca. Only this root is then trusted for the CA's endpoint.

challenges.description: Challenge types to use, in order of preference.

dns_propagation_timeout.description: How long to wait for a DNS-01 record to become visible; the CA validates anyway after.

dns_provider.description:
DNS provider (a key of `dns_providers`) used for every route that does not name one:
all certificates are then validated with DNS-01.

dns_providers.description: DNS providers for DNS-01, referenced by routes.

dns_resolvers.description:
Resolvers (`ip` or `ip:port`) that must see a DNS-01 record before the CA is asked to
validate. By default the zone's authoritative nameservers are asked.

eab.description: External account binding, required by some CAs.

email.description: Contact address for the CA account (optional for Let's Encrypt).

profile.description:
Certificate profile (Let's Encrypt): `classic` (90 days), `tlsserver` (45 days) or
`shortlived` (about 6 days, needed for IP addresses).

staging.description: Use the CA's staging environment (untrusted certificates, high rate limits).

storage.description: Where accounts and certificates are stored. Defaults to `$RDOCK_DATA_DIR/acme`.

oneOf.description: About 6-day certificates; the only profile that allows IP addresses.

anyOf.description: `true` uses the defaults; `false` turns automatic certificates off.

rdock.AcmeSetting.description: The `acme` section: `false` turns automatic certificates off, `true` or settings keep them on.

expected_body.description: Text the response body must contain (HTTP).

grpc_service.description: gRPC service name to check; empty checks the whole server.

healthy.description: Consecutive successes before a backend is healthy.

hostname.description: `Host` of the probe (HTTP); the backend address when unset.

port.description: Probe this port instead of the backend's.

unhealthy.description: Consecutive failures before a backend is unhealthy.

allowed_hosts.description:
Host names the admin listener answers to; other `Host` headers get 421 (DNS-rebinding
defence). Default: `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and `::1` on loopback, the listener's IP
otherwise. Required when `listener` is on all interfaces.

api_writes.description:
Allow configuration changes through the admin API and the dashboard. Set `false`
(`GitOps`) when Git and the file provider are the only source of truth.

dashboard.description: Serve the embedded dashboard on the admin listener.

listener.description: Address of the admin API. Loopback by default; any other address needs `tls`.

metrics_unauthenticated_on_loopback.description:
Serve `/metrics` without a token when the listener is a loopback address, as before
v0.5, for scrapers on the same machine that cannot send one.

mfa.description: Who must use a second factor (TOTP) to log in.

sessions.description: How long a dashboard login lasts.

socket.description:
Unix socket for the local CLI (`rdock reload`, `rdock status`), mode 0600. Default:
`$RDOCK_DATA_DIR/admin.sock`.

threads.description: Worker threads of the admin runtime, kept apart from the proxy's (1–16).

tls.description: TLS for the admin listener. Required when `listener` is not a loopback address.

tokens.description: API tokens for scripts and Prometheus.

trust_forwarded_on_loopback.description:
Take the client's address from `X-Forwarded-For` on connections from loopback. Turn it
on only when a route of this rdock forwards to the admin listener, so rate limits and
token networks see real clients; any local process could otherwise claim an address.

rdock.AdminAudit.description:
The audit log (ADR-0024): every admin write, login, MFA event, refusal and session end, as
JSON lines that each carry the SHA-256 of the line before.

forward.description: Also send each record to a syslog server.

max_file_size.description: A file is closed and a new one started at this size (1 MiB–1 GiB).

retention.description: How long rotated files are kept (1d–3650d).

rdock.AdminPasswords.description:
Password rules for dashboard users (ADR-0024). There are no composition rules: length and
a list of common passwords are what protect a password (NIST SP 800-63B §3.1.1.2).

argon2.description:
Argon2id cost. Values below the OWASP minimum are refused; existing hashes are
upgraded at the next login after a change.

blocklist_file.description:
A file with one password per line (for example a breached-password list) refused in
addition to the bundled list of common passwords. Read once at start, offline.

min_length.description: Shortest password accepted, in characters (8–128). The longest is 128.

rdock.AdminSessions.description:
Dashboard session lifetimes (ADR-0024; OWASP Session Management Cheat Sheet, checked
2026-10-31). Both are between 5 minutes and 12 hours.

absolute.description: A session ends this long after login, however active.

idle.description: A session without requests for this long ends.

rdock.AdminTls.description: Certificate and key the admin listener presents.

allow_no_expiry.description: Allow tokens that never expire. Off by default: a leaked token should stop working.

default_expiry_days.description: Lifetime of a new token when its creator gives none, in days (1–365).

rdock.AlertChannel.description:
One alert destination (ADR-0024). URLs, secrets and passwords are secrets: write them as
`${file:…}` or `${env:…}` references.

Anything that takes Slack's payload: Discord's `/slack` endpoint, Mattermost,

allow_private_targets.description: Allow private, loopback and link-local addresses (an internal relay).

rules.description: Only these rules; all when empty.

Admin security events: login lockouts, user and second-factor changes, tokens used

rdock.AlertRules.description:
What raises alerts. Certificates, backends, config and security are on; the thresholds are
off until set.

error_rate.description: Alert when a service's 5xx share over the window is above this, in percent.

latency.description: Alert when a service's p99 over the window is above this.

channels.description: Where alerts go, by a name you choose.

min_interval.description: The same alert is sent again at most this often while it keeps firing.

webhook.description: Receives each alert as a JSON `POST` (v0.3); works like a `webhook` channel.

rdock.Argon2Cost.description:
Argon2id parameters. The default is the OWASP minimum, m=19456 KiB, t=2, p=1 (Password
Storage Cheat Sheet, checked 2026-10-31).

ca_file.description: CA that signed the syslog server's certificate, for `tls`; the system's CAs when unset.

syslog.description:
Syslog server as `host:port`; records are RFC 5424 messages with the JSON record as
the message.

transport.description:
`udp` (default), `tcp` (octet counting, RFC 6587) or `tls` (RFC 5425). Only `tls`
protects records on the network.

backup.description: Only used when no primary backend is available.

rdock.ByteSize.description: Size in bytes, optionally with a unit (KB = 1000, KiB = 1024).

rdock.Certificate.description:
A certificate and private key provided as files. Changes to the files are picked up
automatically.

key_file.description: PEM private key (PKCS#8, PKCS#1 or SEC1; PKCS#8 may be encrypted).

key_password.description:
Password of an encrypted key. Reference a secret instead of writing it here:
`"${file:/run/secrets/key_password}"`.

oneOf.description: DNS-01 through a DNS provider; needed for wildcard certificates.

ca_files.description: PEM files with the CA certificates that sign client certificates.

cloudflare.description: Also trust Cloudflare's CA for global Authenticated Origin Pulls.

mode.description:
`required` refuses handshakes without a valid certificate; `optional` accepts them
without one, but verifies a certificate that is sent.

rdock.ClientAuthMode.description: Whether a client certificate is required.

oneOf.description: Every connection needs a valid certificate.
A certificate is optional; routes can demand one with the `client_cert` middleware.

rdock.ClientCertForward.description:
How a client certificate is passed to the backend. Copies of these headers sent by clients
are always removed.

oneOf.description:
`CF-Connecting-IP` when the peer is in Cloudflare's ranges, otherwise the right-most
untrusted `X-Forwarded-For` entry.

`CF-Connecting-IP` from a trusted proxy (Cloudflare's edge or a listed network); needs
`cloudflare` in `trusted_proxies`.

rdock.Config.description:
A complete ReverseDock configuration, as written in `rdock.yaml`.

Every section is optional. Names of listeners, routes, services, middlewares and
certificates are map keys; other objects refer to them by name.

Automatic certificates (ACME). On by default with Let's Encrypt, HTTP-01 and TLS-ALPN-01;
`false` turns it off.

defaults.description: Defaults applied to routes that do not set a value.

listeners.description:
Sockets to accept traffic on. When empty, `web` (`:80`) and `websecure` (`:443`, TLS)
are used.

providers.description: Dynamic configuration sources (file, Docker, Swarm, Kubernetes).

routes.description: HTTP routes: which requests go to which service, through which middlewares.

security.description: Client IP trust and request limits.

services.description: Backend pools that routes send traffic to.

tcp_routes.description: TCP routes (SNI routing, passthrough, plain TCP).

version.description: Configuration format version. Only `1` exists; omit it to use the latest.

rdock.Config.title: ReverseDock configuration (rdock.yaml)

certificate.description:
Certificate (a key of `certificates`) served when no other certificate matches the
requested name, or when the client sends no name (SNI).

listeners.description: Listeners used by routes that do not name any.

redirect_http_to_https.description: Redirect plain HTTP requests to HTTPS for hosts that have a TLS route.

tls.description: TLS for routes that do not set `tls`: `auto` (automatic certificates) or `off`.

rdock.DnsProvider.description: A DNS provider for DNS-01 challenges.

oneOf.description: Cloudflare DNS, with an API token allowed to edit the zone's DNS records.

zone_id.description: Zone ID. Looked up from the name when omitted, which also needs Zone → Zone → Read.

oneOf.description: A program run as `<command> <args…> present|cleanup <name> <value>`, without a shell.

endpoint.description: Docker Engine API endpoint. Read-only access is enough; a socket proxy is recommended.

entrypoints.description: Traefik entrypoint name → listener name, for Traefik labels.

expose_by_default.description: Expose containers without `rdock.enable=true`. Off by default.

host_address.description: Address used for containers in host network mode.

network.description: Network used to reach containers that are on several networks.

rdock.Duration.description: Duration made of numbers with units: ms, s, m, h, d.

min_requests.description: Fewer requests than this in the window never alert.

hmac_key.description: Base64url HMAC key from the CA. Reference a secret instead of writing it here.

rdock.HeaderRules.description: Header operations, applied in the order remove, set, add.

slow_start.description: A backend that becomes healthy ramps up its weight over this time.

when_all_down.description: What happens when no backend is healthy.

rdock.HealthMode.description: How a probe checks a backend.

oneOf.description: An HTTP request with the service's scheme.

`Strict-Transport-Security` settings. Browsers then refuse plain HTTP for the host, so
enable it only when HTTPS works for every name involved.

include_subdomains.description: Apply the policy to all subdomains too.

max_age.description: How long browsers remember the policy. `0s` removes it.

preload.description: Ask for inclusion in browser preload lists. This is hard to undo.

oneOf.description: Buypass Go SSL: discontinued on 2025-10-16 and refused by validation.

namespaces.description: Namespaces to watch; all when empty.

min_requests.description: Fewer requests than this in the window never alert.

p99.description: The p99 above which a service alerts.

oneOf.description:
Fewest requests in flight relative to the weight (an HTTP/1.1 request holds one
connection, so this is also the least-connections policy).
Fewest requests in flight relative to the weight.
Consistent hash of the client IP (Traefik's `hrw`).
Consistent hash of a request header (`hash_on`).

drain_timeout.description:
On shutdown, how long open requests may finish before connections are closed. Keep it
below the supervisor's stop timeout (Docker waits 10 s before it kills the process).

rdock.Limits.description: Request size limits. Requests over a limit are answered with 431, 414 or 413.

max_body_bytes.description: Request body size, also enforced for chunked bodies. Unlimited when omitted.

max_header_bytes.description: Total size of the request line and headers.

max_in_flight.description:
Requests in flight across every listener; more are answered `503` with `Retry-After`

upstream_idle_connections.description:
Idle keep-alive connections to backends kept per listener for reuse. Connections
beyond it are closed when their request ends, so a busy listener keeps opening new
ones. Applies to listeners started after the change.

rdock.ListenAddress.description: Listen address: `:port` for all interfaces, or `ip:port`.

rdock.Listener.description: A socket ReverseDock accepts connections on.

ping.description:
A path answered `200 OK` for any host before routing, for load-balancer health
monitors such as Cloudflare Load Balancing, e.g. `/rdock/ping`.

protocol.description: Protocol. Inferred when omitted: `https` if `tls` is set, otherwise `http`.

proxy_protocol.description: Accept the PROXY protocol (v1 or v2) from these sources only.

oneOf.description: Raw TCP, optionally with TLS termination or SNI passthrough.

rdock.ListenerTimeouts.description: Timeouts for the client side of a listener.

idle.description: How long an idle keep-alive connection is kept open.

read.description: Longest wait for data from the client while a request or upgraded connection is open.

request_header.description:
Time allowed to receive the complete request headers, counted from their first byte
(protects against slow-header attacks).

write.description: Longest wait for the client to accept data.

client_auth.description: Client certificates (mTLS). A certificate is always verified against these roots.

hash_on.description: Header or cookie name for `header_hash` and `cookie_hash`.

Authentication endpoint. A 2xx answer allows the request; anything else is returned to

trust_forward_header.description: Trust `X-Forwarded-*` headers already present on the request.
